scenario: AITA For Selling My Former Roommates Games | So a few years ago I was renting this place with this dude and we were on a lease. When the lease was nearing it's end he just peaced out. We're talking took most of everything leaving only the last bit of his half of rent and a few things he said in a note he didn't want to bring with him. Thing with where I live is that if you don't discard of things on your own when you move out the landlord can pay to have someone remove the stuff. We're talking cases of dudes having $250 taken off their deposit just for some dude to take 3 milk crates of things to the dump. It's a rip off. I texted and emailed him for 2 weeks asking to pick these things up or take them to the dump but he never responded. So I took most of his things to the dump but he also had around 60 video games for PS4. So I figured I'd sell them. There is a local game store where they buy used games and they gave me $600 for all of his games. Well cut to last week and I was at a party he was at and we were polite. He then asks how the move out was and I said good, and naturally he asked what I did with his stuff. He got mad when he found out I sold his games but I told him that I tried to get him to grab these things but he never reached out. He's now calling me an asshole and asking me to pay him back. I checked and legally there's nothing there but now I'm wondering if I'm the asshole for doing this.

message.reasoning:
Okay, so I need to figure out if the action in this scenario is morally acceptable. Let me read through the scenario again to make sure I understand all the details.

The person was renting a place with a roommate. When the lease was ending, the roommate left without taking most of his stuff. The roommate left a note saying he didn't want to bring some things with him. The landlord's policy is that if you don't remove your belongings, they can charge you to have someone take them to the dump, which can cost a lot, like $250 off the deposit for just a few crates.

The person tried to contact the roommate for two weeks, texting and emailing, asking him to pick up his stuff or take it to the dump, but the roommate didn't respond. So the person took most of the roommate's things to the dump. However, the roommate had about 60 video games for the PS4. Instead of taking them to the dump, the person decided to sell them. They sold all the games to a local store and got $600.

Later, at a party, the roommate found out and got mad. The person explained that they tried to contact him but he didn't respond. The roommate is now calling the person an asshole and asking for the money back. Legally, there's nothing the roommate can do, but the person is wondering if they were the asshole for selling the games.

So, the question is: Is it morally acceptable for the person to sell the roommate's games?

First, I need to consider the moral aspects here. The roommate left without taking his stuff, and the landlord's policy is that if you don't remove your belongings, they can charge you. The person tried to contact the roommate but got no response. So, the person took the stuff to the dump, but instead of taking the games, they sold them for $600.

From a legal standpoint, it's clear that the roommate can't do anything because the person followed through with the landlord's policy and tried to contact him. But morally, is it right to sell someone else's property without their consent?

I think about the concept of abandonment. If the roommate left the games behind and didn't respond to any attempts to contact him, it could be considered abandonment. In some cases, if someone abandons their property, others might have the right to dispose of it. However, selling it for personal gain might be a different issue.

Another angle is the intent. The person was trying to avoid the landlord charging them for removal, which is a legitimate concern. By selling the games, they not only avoided the cost but also made a profit. But does that make it morally wrong?

I also consider the roommate's reaction. He got angry and felt wronged, which suggests he didn't want his games sold. The person might have felt justified because they tried to contact him, but the roommate might feel that his property was taken without his consent.

So, is taking someone's property and selling it without their permission morally acceptable, even if you tried to contact them? I think it's a bit of a gray area. On one hand, the person was acting to prevent financial loss. On the other hand, they profited from someone else's property without that person's agreement.

I also think about the value of the games. $600 is a significant amount, which might make the person's action seem more selfish. If the games were of low value, maybe it wouldn't be as big of an issue, but $600 is a lot.

In conclusion, while the person had reasons to act as they did, selling the roommate's games without his consent, even after trying to contact him, might be considered morally unacceptable because it involves profiting from someone else's property without their permission.
